# The settings template lets a seat discard its own working-tree edits: allow `git checkout --` and `git restore`

## Context

`.claude/settings.template.json` is the permissions source every Claude seat's real `.claude/settings.json` is derived from (five Claude peers today). Its `permissions.allow` names the git verbs a seat may run without a prompt: `git add`, `git commit`, `git checkout -b agent/*`, `git checkout dev`, `git fetch`, `git status`, `git log`, `git diff`, `git branch`, `git rev-list`, `git rev-parse`, `git merge-base`, `git show`, `git push --force-with-lease origin agent/*`, plus the `gh pr` / `gh issue` reads. Discarding a seat's own uncommitted edits is not among them, and the force-push row names a branch prefix (`agent/*`) no seat uses any more (`clio/*`, `ada/*`, …).

## The Problem

On 2026-09-26 the auto-mode classifier refused `git checkout -- a.spec.mjs b.spec.mjs c.spec.mjs` — three spec edits the seat had made minutes earlier in the same session — as "Irreversible Local Destruction", and its wording forbids the same outcome through any other route (Edit, stash, restore, re-issued flags). The seat cannot undo its own work-in-progress the way a developer does a dozen times a day; it must either design forward around the dead end or stop and ask the operator. The same layer judges every force push to a seat's own feature branch, although every PR is squash-merged to `dev` and a feature branch's history is the seat's alone. The operator approved both allowances on 2026-09-26 ("approved on my end"; "force pushes into feature branches are fine too => we squash merge every PR to dev") and asked for them to land in the template first, so all five seats inherit them, and for the real settings files to be updated from the template afterwards.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.claude/settings.template.json` — `permissions.allow` (the rows above) and `permissions.deny` (`gh pr merge`, force pushes to `dev` / `main` in both spellings, refspec pushes, plain pushes to `dev` / `main`, `--no-verify`, `Workflow`); the file also carries the rationale for the subagent / fan-out denial (`AGENTS.md §swarm_topology_anchor`).
- Deny rows win over allow rows, so a broad force-push allowance stays fenced by the existing `dev` / `main` deny rows.
- The classifier is a layer above the rules: a command an allow row matches is not sent to it, which is what the denial text points at ("the user can add a Bash permission rule to their settings").
- The real per-seat `.claude/settings.json` files are the operator's (security settings); they are updated from the template after this lands, not by this ticket.
- Structure map: N/A (repository configuration).

## The Fix

In `.claude/settings.template.json`, in the file's existing glob style beside the other git rows:

```json
"Bash(git checkout -- *)",
"Bash(git restore *)",
"Bash(git rebase *)",
"Bash(git push --force-with-lease origin *)",
"Bash(git push --force origin *)"
```

and the `agent/*`-scoped force-push row goes, superseded by the broad one. `git checkout -- <paths>` and `git restore <paths>` discard uncommitted changes to the named paths only. `git rebase` rewrites the seat's own branch history and is what a force push exists for; without it the allowance is half. The force-push rows cover feature branches only because `permissions.deny` already refuses `--force*` / `-f` pushes to `dev*` and `main*` and every refspec push — those deny rows stay exactly as they are. `git stash` stays out: a different outcome (parked work that can be forgotten) nobody asked for.

## Decision Record impact

none — permission rows, no process or topology change; the squash-merge policy is the operator's standing practice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `.claude/settings.template.json` carries `Bash(git checkout -- *)`, `Bash(git restore *)`, `Bash(git rebase *)`, `Bash(git push --force-with-lease origin *)` and `Bash(git push --force origin *)` in `permissions.allow` beside the existing git rows, the `agent/*` force-push row removed, every `dev` / `main` deny row unchanged, and the file still parses as JSON.
- [ ] AC-2 The PR body names the operator's approvals (2026-09-26, both quotes above) and states that the per-seat `.claude/settings.json` files are updated from the template by the operator afterwards.

## Out of Scope

The per-seat settings files (the operator's); `git stash`; branch-creation rules (`git checkout -b agent/*` stays as it is).

## Related

The classifier's denial pattern also refuses raw `gh api graphql` mutations (the MCP write tools are the route there) — same layer, separate rule, not this ticket.
